instructions: Generate a topic only from an explicit compatibilityGroup; do not form a Cartesian product from taxonomy arrays.
Apply every matching compatibilityRule before selecting a product series or making a process recommendation.
Treat confirmed-internal mappings as selection starting points that still require production-representative sampling.
Treat uncertain-internal mappings as research or qualification topics, never as product-performance claims.

substrates.label: Coated paper
qualificationNotes: Record coating, ink, varnish, smoothness, and cure state before selecting a grade.

substrates.label: Uncoated paper
qualificationNotes: Absorbency and surface roughness can change transfer completeness and gloss.

substrates.label: Textured or specialty paper
qualificationNotes: Texture depth, compressibility, and large-area coverage must be sampled together.

substrates.label: Kraft paper or board
qualificationNotes: Surface variation and background color make opacity and adhesion job-specific.

substrates.label: Folding carton board
qualificationNotes: Use the printed, varnished, or laminated production construction for approval.

substrates.label: Rigid gift-box wrap or board
qualificationNotes: Qualify the wrap material separately from the underlying board and adhesive construction.

substrates.label: Laminated paper or paperboard
qualificationNotes: Identify the film chemistry and treatment; similar-looking laminates are not interchangeable.

substrates.label: Paper label facestock
qualificationNotes: Facestock coating, print, varnish, and converting speed belong in the same trial record.

substrates.label: Film label facestock
qualificationNotes: Identify polymer, primer, corona history, ink system, and heat tolerance.

substrates.label: ABS
qualificationNotes: Mold release, additives, coating, and part geometry can change adhesion.

substrates.label: Polystyrene (PS)
qualificationNotes: Confirm heat tolerance and part deformation at production dwell and pressure.

substrates.label: Rigid PVC
qualificationNotes: Plasticizer, coating, and heat history require grade-specific testing.

substrates.label: PMMA (acrylic)
qualificationNotes: Check coating, stress sensitivity, geometry, and cosmetic durability requirements.

substrates.label: PET or PETG film/component
qualificationNotes: Distinguish film facestock, laminate, and molded component; they are separate constructions.

substrates.label: Polypropylene (PP)
qualificationNotes: Surface treatment and surface-energy verification are normally part of qualification; no universal grade is implied.

substrates.label: Polyethylene (PE)
qualificationNotes: Resin grade, additives, treatment decay, and flexibility make adhesion strongly system-dependent.

substrates.label: Natural leather
qualificationNotes: Tannery finish, oils, texture, thickness, and heat response vary; test each leather lot.

substrates.label: PU synthetic leather
qualificationNotes: Topcoat and texture must be identified; PU constructions are not interchangeable.

substrates.label: PVC synthetic leather or book cover
qualificationNotes: Plasticizer, finish, and heat response require a representative sample.

substrates.label: Coated glass container
qualificationNotes: Internal notes mention glass, but coating and equipment details are unresolved; treat as a qualification topic, not a default PC claim.

tests.label: Controlled process-window sampling
tests.scopeNote: Change one recorded variable at a time on production-representative material; supplier settings are starting points only.

tests.label: Visual transfer-completeness inspection
tests.scopeNote: Define viewing conditions and acceptance examples before testing.

tests.label: Magnified edge and fine-detail inspection
tests.scopeNote: Use the production artwork and agreed minimum features.

tests.label: Job-specific tape pull
tests.scopeNote: Record tape, pressure, dwell, peel angle, peel rate, conditioning, and acceptance criterion; do not call it a standards test unless the full standard applies.

tests.label: Agreed cross-cut classification
tests.scopeNote: ISO 2409 and ASTM D3359 have defined scopes and limitations; confirm applicability to the complete decoration system before citing either method.

tests.label: Dry rub or abrasion comparison
tests.scopeNote: Specify load, receptor, cycles, conditioning, and pass/fail criterion.

tests.label: Alcohol or specified-agent rub test
tests.scopeNote: Specify agent, concentration, applicator, load, cycles, dwell, and visual acceptance; avoid a generic 'alcohol resistant' claim.

tests.label: Agreed scratch-resistance test
tests.scopeNote: Select a method suitable for the decorated article and define whether the result is pass/fail or comparative.

tests.label: Fold or crease durability
tests.scopeNote: Use the production board grain, crease geometry, and post-stamp sequence.

tests.label: Registration and pitch measurement
tests.scopeNote: Set tolerances from artwork, repeat length, sensor, equipment, and security specification.

tests.label: Color and gloss comparison to approved master
tests.scopeNote: Keep substrate, lighting, viewing geometry, and instrument method consistent.

tests.label: Surface-energy or wetting check
tests.scopeNote: Use as a process-control indicator, not as proof that a particular foil grade will adhere.

tests.label: Repeat-run and batch stability check
tests.scopeNote: Retain approved samples and setup records, then compare substrate and foil batches under controlled settings.

productSeries.label: PK Brown Back Series
uncertainties: The public catalog does not map individual PK color codes to substrate-specific adhesive/release grades.
Leather and difficult coatings are grade- and finish-specific despite being named in internal product evidence.
No numeric temperature, adhesion, or durability claim should be generated without a current technical data sheet and sample approval.

productSeries.label: PC Plastic/Cold Foils Series
uncertainties: Internal sources mention both plastic hot-stamping grades and cold/digital variants; membership in PC alone does not prove cold-foil compatibility.
PP and PE require treatment and application-specific qualification and must not be described as universally compatible.
The internal glass reference lacks coating and equipment detail and is excluded from confirmed substrate mappings.
Alcohol resistance requires a named method and acceptance criterion; the series name alone is not evidence of a pass.

productSeries.label: PL/PY Pigment Foils
uncertainties: Internal sources consistently support paper and packaging uses but differ on the breadth of plastics and leather compatibility.
PL is glossy and PY is matte in the current catalog grouping; exact opacity, color match, and grade suitability require sampling.
Do not generate plastics or leather recommendations for PLPY unless an individual grade is qualified.

productSeries.label: Digital / Cold Foil
uncertainties: DIGITAL exists in PINTE category content but has no item-level entries in data/foil_data.ts.
MGI, Scodix, toner, UV-varnish, screen-printed adhesive, narrow-web, and sheet-fed cold transfer are distinct systems and cannot share a blanket compatibility claim.
Generate DIGITAL content as process qualification and procurement guidance until grade-level technical data is available.

compatibilityRules.rationale: Industry, substrate, treatment, process, artwork, defect, and region arrays are vocabularies, not independent dimensions.
Compatibility and settings depend on the actual substrate construction, machine, artwork, speed, and acceptance method.
Fine detail, large solids, rough stock, plastics, and leather can require different release and adhesive behavior.
Cold transfer depends on a matched adhesive, substrate, foil, curing, nip, and printing system.
Low-surface-energy plastics and treatment decay make adhesion application-specific.
Internal sources mention PC cold/digital variants but do not make every PC catalog item a cold-transfer foil.
The DIGITAL category has internal descriptions but no item-level entries in the current foil catalog.
Internal evidence is consistent for paper packaging but inconsistent or broad for plastics and leather.
The internal glass reference lacks coating, grade, and equipment detail.
A diffraction or rainbow effect is decorative unless controlled security features and verification requirements are specified.
Security performance depends on feature design, controlled origination, production, registration, and verification, not appearance alone.
Standards and shop tests have defined substrates, apparatus, conditioning, and limitations; the buyer and supplier must agree what applies.
The same visible defect can arise from substrate, foil, machine, artwork, or process variables.
A geographic market is not evidence that a foil, substrate, or process combination is compatible or compliant.
